title: CouncilLens people model
description: The contract for the 'who runs the council' layer: one file per council, written by the analyse stage to data/analysed/<council-slug>/people.json. It answers who sits on the council, how long they have been there, what roles they hold, what they have declared about themselves, and who the senior officers are. Strict: unknown fields are rejected. Everything in it comes from the council's own publications or from a councillor's own sworn declaration under the Localism Act 2011. Nothing here may be assembled by matching a name against an outside database, a social network or the press, and nothing may record family, health or a home address.

source_ids.description: Canonical record ids this output was derived from.

review_status.description: needs_review: unchecked. ai_reviewed: independently checked against the source documents by a second AI pass, not yet by a person. reviewed: checked by a person.

cache_key.description: sha256 over the item key, the sha256 of each source document's extracted text, and the prompt version. Same rule as the topic model — see src/analyse/README.md.

date_string.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Null when the record gives no date at all.

text.description: The councillor's own words from the register, shortened but never reworded. Names of employers and organisations only — never an address, a family member, or anything the register does not itself carry.

category.description: The heading the register itself put this under, e.g. 'Employment, office, trade or profession'.

composition.description: How the seats are shared out, as the council's own directory shows them on the date it was read.

party.description: The party label the council itself prints.

next_election_note.description: What the council says about when the next election is, or null if it does not say.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences a 14-year-old can follow.

councillors.description: One entry per sitting councillor, in the order the council's own directory lists them.

party.description: The party label the council prints. Null where the council prints none.

current_term_start.description: The start of the term they are serving now, as the council's directory gives it.

elections.description: Every election the council's own record shows them winning, oldest first. Votes and majority only where the council publishes a result sheet.

roles.description: Jobs inside the council: Leader, a Cabinet portfolio, a committee chair, Lord Mayor, and so on.

body_slug.description: The committee or body the role belongs to, where there is one.

committees.description: Committees they currently sit on, by the slug used in `bodies`.

role.description: As the council prints it: Member, Chair, Vice Chair, Substitute.

outside_bodies.description: Organisations the council itself appointed them to. Not a private interest — an appointment the council made and publishes.

attendance.description: Null where the council does not publish attendance in a form that can be read. A null is an honest answer, not a missing value to be guessed at.

allowances.description: What the council's published allowances schedule says this councillor was entitled to or paid. Null where no per-councillor figure is published.

interests.description: The councillor's own declaration, made under the Localism Act 2011 and published by the council. Reproduced in their words, shortened, never rewritten and never interpreted. `land` carries ward-level detail only: never a street address.

land.description: Ward-level only, e.g. 'Land and property in the Mancroft ward'. A street address must never appear here.

note.description: Plain sentence on what could and could not be read, e.g. that the register is published only as a date-stamped notice.

declared_links.description: Websites the councillor asked the council to print on their own council page. Recorded as the council prints them and never fetched, followed or read by this project.

contact.description: The council contact route only. Personal telephone numbers are deliberately not carried, even where the council prints them.

address.description: The council's own care-of address, e.g. 'c/o City Hall, Norwich'. Never a home address.

summary.description: Two or three plain sentences a 14-year-old can follow. Non-judgmental: what the record says, never what to think about it.

officers.description: Paid senior staff, as published under the Local Government Transparency Code. Officers are employees, not politicians: only role, published name, published pay band and statutory duty are carried.

role.description: The post, as the council titles it.

name.description: Only where the council itself publishes the post-holder's name. Null otherwise.

statutory_role.description: The duty in law this post carries, where the council says it carries one.

pay_band.description: As published, e.g. '£120,000 - £124,999'. Never a calculated or estimated figure.

bodies.description: Committees and panels, so a topic page can say which councillors sit on the committee that decided it.

purpose.description: One plain sentence on what it decides, drawn from the council's own description.

gaps.description: What we looked for about this council's people and could not find published. A gap is a fact about the council's publishing, not a failure of the build.
